en: His lion Bakai Khan was not there.
Companions even in the hereafter,
All those forty champions were absent.
His hapless eyes drooped shut,
His looks faded, his belly burned,
His strength left him as he languished.
Once Közkaman had become his enemy,
My sultan openly despaired of life.
Unable to rise, doubled over,
After drinking the accursed poison,
My sultan fell straight onto his head.
“For not heeding Kanykei's words,
Let this poor head suffer on,” he said.
My dear lord grieved.
Kökchököz's nine sons,
Közkaman's nine sons—
All were masters of the spear,
Skilled men who knew the enemy's tactics,
Marksmen whose shots did not miss,
All warriors hostile to your father.
From the khan of the khagan's people
Those bold men had willingly come,
Warriors with cast-iron heads,
